``` r
library(estilex)
```

This vignette is pre-computed. Every result below was produced by a real
request to the Riigi Teataja, but the code is not run when the package is
built or checked, so neither CRAN nor your own `R CMD check` needs a network
connection. The source with live calls is `vignettes/estilex.Rmd.orig`.

## What estilex covers

The Riigi Teataja is Estonia's official legal gazette. Its public API, in
service since June 2026, serves consolidated texts of acts and regulations
as JSON and XML, together with their amendment histories and their English
translations.

estilex wraps that API and adds the parts it does not provide: a document
model in tidy tibbles, text rendered with its structure intact, and a join
between the Estonian and English versions of an act at section level.

What the API does not offer is search. There is no endpoint that answers
"which acts mention X", and none that lists what exists. Identifiers come
from somewhere else, which the last section of this vignette deals with.

## Identifiers

A document is addressed by a twelve-digit identifier, visible in the
address of any Riigi Teataja page. The format encodes a type digit, a date
and a sequence number:

```
111042025003  ->  1 | 11 | 04 | 2025 | 003
```

A leading `5` marks an English translation. estilex uses that to route the
request, because translations live on a separate path.

The identifier names one consolidated version, not the act in general. Every
amendment produces a new one. Older versions keep their own identifiers and
can be retrieved exactly as the current one, which is how point-in-time work
is done with this package.

Identifiers are handled as character throughout. They fit in a double, but
they are identifiers rather than numbers, and leading digits matter.

The running example is the Constitution of the Republic of Estonia,
`111042025003`.

## A document


``` r
doc <- etx_get_doc("111042025003")

doc$status
#> [1] "ok"
doc$pealkiri
#> [1] "Eesti Vabariigi põhiseadus"
doc$kehtivuse_algus
#> [1] "2026-02-28"
```

Column names follow the source language, as elsewhere in lexverse, so that a
field in the output can be traced back to a field in the published XML
without a translation table:


``` r
names(doc)
#>  [1] "status"             "id"                 "kehtiv_id"         
#>  [4] "grupi_id"           "pealkiri"           "lyhend"            
#>  [7] "tekstiliik"         "dokumentliik"       "akti_staatus"      
#> [10] "kehtivus_staatus"   "kehtivuse_algus"    "kehtivuse_lopp"    
#> [13] "avaldamise_kuupaev" "is_translation"     "tolke_seos_id"     
#> [16] "tolke_seos_tekst"   "liigitused"         "n_viited"          
#> [19] "source_url"         "error_message"
```

Retrieval never throws on a document that cannot be fetched. The `status`
column carries the outcome instead:


``` r
bad <- etx_get_doc("999999999999")
bad$status
#> [1] "not_found"
bad$error_message
#> [1] NA
```

This matters when a list of identifiers is processed in a loop, which is the
normal case. One missing document should not end the run.

## Text

`etx_get_text()` returns the whole text as a single string, with chapter and
section headings in place:


``` r
txt <- etx_get_text("111042025003")
nchar(txt$text)
#> [1] 54343
cat(substr(txt$text, 1, 450))
#> Kõikumatus usus ja vankumatus tahtes kindlustada ja arendada riiki,
#> mis on loodud Eesti rahva riikliku enesemääramise kustumatul õigusel ja välja kuulutatud 1918. aasta 24. veebruaril,
#> mis on rajatud vabadusele, õiglusele ja õigusele,
#> mis on kaitseks sisemisele ja välisele rahule ning pandiks praegustele ja tulevastele põlvedele nende ühiskondlikus edus ja üldises kasus,
#> mis peab tagama eesti rahvuse, keele ja kultuuri säilimise läbi aegade –
#> võt
```

`etx_get_paragraphs()` returns the same content one provision per row, with
chapter context on each:


``` r
par <- etx_get_paragraphs("111042025003")
dim(par)
#> [1] 324  12
names(par)
#>  [1] "id"               "is_translation"   "peatykk_nr"       "peatykk"         
#>  [5] "peatykk_pealkiri" "paragrahv_index"  "paragrahv_nr"     "paragrahv"       
#>  [9] "loige_index"      "n_alampunkt"      "text"             "source_url"
```


``` r
par[par$paragrahv_nr == "10", c("peatykk_nr", "peatykk_pealkiri",
                                "paragrahv", "text")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   peatykk_nr peatykk_pealkiri                     paragrahv text                
#>   <chr>      <chr>                                <chr>     <chr>               
#> 1 II         PÕHIÕIGUSED, VABADUSED JA KOHUSTUSED § 10.     Käesolevas peatükis…
```

Chapters are available by grouping:


``` r
tapply(par$paragrahv_nr, par$peatykk_pealkiri, function(x) length(unique(x)))
#>                  KOHALIK OMAVALITSUS                                KOHUS 
#>                                    7                                    8 
#>                        ÕIGUSKANTSLER PÕHIÕIGUSED, VABADUSED JA KOHUSTUSED 
#>                                    7                                   48 
#>                 PÕHISEADUSE MUUTMINE             RAHANDUS JA RIIGIEELARVE 
#>                                    8                                    9 
#>                               RAHVAS                          RIIGIKAITSE 
#>                                    3                                    8 
#>                            RIIGIKOGU                        RIIGIKONTROLL 
#>                                   18                                    7 
#>                         SEADUSANDLUS                  VABARIIGI PRESIDENT 
#>                                    2                                    9 
#>                   VABARIIGI VALITSUS         VÄLISSUHTED JA VÄLISLEPINGUD 
#>                                   16                                    4 
#>                            ÜLDSÄTTED 
#>                                    7
```

Sub-point markers such as `1)` are kept inline in the text. Estonian
cross-references cite sub-points, so removing the markers would cost more
than the noise they add.

## Amendment history

Each amendment leaves a `muutmismärge` in the XML. These sit at two levels:
some record an amendment to the act, others to a single section.


``` r
ref <- etx_get_references("111042025003")
dim(ref)
#> [1] 16 13
names(ref)
#>  [1] "id"           "ref_index"    "scope_nr"     "scope"        "akt_viide"   
#>  [6] "akti_kuupaev" "joustumine"   "rt_osa"       "rt_aasta"     "rt_nr"       
#> [11] "rt_artikkel"  "rt_viide"     "source_url"
```

`scope_nr` gives the section an entry attaches to, or `NA` for an entry at
document level:


``` r
table(document_level = is.na(ref$scope_nr))
#> document_level
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>     9     7
```


``` r
ref[!is.na(ref$scope_nr), c("scope_nr", "akti_kuupaev", "joustumine",
                            "rt_viide")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   scope_nr akti_kuupaev joustumine rt_viide          
#>   <chr>    <date>       <date>     <chr>             
#> 1 65       NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 2 74       NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 3 78       NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 4 78       NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 5 78       NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 6 127      NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 7 128      NA           2011-07-22 RT I 1            
#> 8 156      NA           2005-10-17 RT I 2003, 29, 174
#> 9 156      NA           2026-03-01 RT I 1
```

`rt_viide` assembles the publication components into the citation form
Estonian legal sources use in print, for example `RT I 2003, 29, 174`. It is
the string to quote in a footnote. The four components are kept separately as
well, in `rt_osa`, `rt_aasta`, `rt_nr` and `rt_artikkel`, which is the form to
use for filtering or for joining against other sources.

The identifier of the amending act is also present, and it uses the same
identifier space as the acts themselves. The citation network is therefore
traversable directly, with no lookup table:


``` r
amending <- ref$akt_viide[!is.na(ref$akt_viide)][1]
amending
#> [1] "550572"
etx_get_doc(amending)$pealkiri
#> [1] "Eesti Vabariigi põhiseaduse muutmise seadus kohaliku omavalitsuse volikogu valimiseks neljaks aastaks"
```

## Translations

An act's English translation, where one exists, is reached through the link
recorded in its metadata:


``` r
tr <- etx_get_translation("111042025003")

tr$status
#> [1] "ok"
tr$pealkiri_en
#> [1] "The Constitution of the Republic of Estonia"
tr$is_current
#> [1] TRUE
cat(substr(tr$text, 1, 350))
#> With unwavering faith and a steadfast will to strengthen and develop the state,
#> which is established on the inextinguishable right of the people of Estonia to national self-determination and which was proclaimed on 24 February 1918,
#> which is founded on liberty, justice and law,
#> which is for the defence of internal and external peace, and is a pledg
```

Three things are worth knowing about these translations.

**They are not official.** Only the Estonian text has legal force in
domestic proceedings. Translations are kept up to date, but they are not
usable as official texts, which is why the Riigi Teataja holds them apart
from the law in force on a separate route. estilex follows that route
automatically.

**Most acts have none.** The English archives hold roughly 6,800 documents
against a far larger body of Estonian legislation.

**Currency is established by comparing validity dates, not publication
dates.** Translations carry no version information of their own, and
publication dates commonly differ by days even when the translation is
current. `is_current` compares `kehtivuse_algus` on both sides:


``` r
tr[, c("kehtivuse_algus", "kehtivuse_algus_en", "is_current")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   kehtivuse_algus kehtivuse_algus_en is_current
#>   <date>          <date>             <lgl>     
#> 1 2026-02-28      2026-03-01         TRUE
```

## Parallel texts

The feature that distinguishes this package. Section numbering is preserved
exactly across languages, so the two versions join on the section number
rather than on position:


``` r
pp <- etx_get_parallel("111042025003")
dim(pp)
#> [1] 168  14
names(pp)
#>  [1] "id"                 "translation_id"     "has_translation"   
#>  [4] "peatykk_nr"         "peatykk_pealkiri"   "paragrahv_nr"      
#>  [7] "paragrahv"          "text_et"            "text_en"           
#> [10] "n_char_et"          "n_char_en"          "kehtivuse_algus"   
#> [13] "kehtivuse_algus_en" "source_url"
```


``` r
pp[pp$paragrahv_nr == "10", c("paragrahv", "text_et", "text_en")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   paragrahv text_et                                                      text_en
#>   <chr>     <chr>                                                        <chr>  
#> 1 § 10.     Käesolevas peatükis loetletud õigused, vabadused ja kohustu… The ri…
```

Subsection counts can differ slightly between languages, so all subsections
of a section are concatenated and the join stops at section level. Aligning
below it would work in most documents and fail silently in others, which is
the worst kind of defect in research use.

A first, crude measure of divergence is length. Estonian is more compact
than English in most registers, so a translation much shorter than its
original is unusual enough to be worth a look:


``` r
ratio <- pp$n_char_en / pp$n_char_et
summary(ratio)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.1993  1.1699  1.2651  1.2781  1.3819  1.7895

head(pp[!is.na(ratio) & ratio < 0.7, c("paragrahv", "n_char_et", "n_char_en")])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   paragrahv n_char_et n_char_en
#>   <chr>         <int>     <int>
#> 1 § 168.          858       171
```

Sections with no translation at all come back as rows with `text_en`
missing, rather than being dropped:


``` r
sum(is.na(pp$text_en))
#> [1] 0
```

That is deliberate. In work on translation fidelity an absent translation is
an observation, not an error, and it is the structure of the Estonian act
that makes the gap measurable.

### Fidelity over time

Riigi Teataja links each consolidated version to the translation that
matches it, rather than always to the newest. The two dates on every row
record which pair was compared:


``` r
unique(pp[, c("id", "translation_id", "kehtivuse_algus",
              "kehtivuse_algus_en")])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   id           translation_id kehtivuse_algus kehtivuse_algus_en
#>   <chr>        <chr>          <date>          <date>            
#> 1 111042025003 523042025002   2026-02-28      2026-03-01
```

Because older versions have identifiers of their own, the same comparison
can be repeated at an earlier point in time, and the result is
contemporaneous rather than anachronistic:


``` r
old <- etx_get_parallel("115052015002")
unique(old[, c("kehtivuse_algus", "kehtivuse_algus_en")])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   kehtivuse_algus kehtivuse_algus_en
#>   <date>          <date>            
#> 1 2015-08-12      2015-08-14
```

Two measurements of the same act, eleven years apart, each against the
translation then in force. No other source in the lexverse family supports
this.

## Finding identifiers

Since the API has no search endpoint, a list of what exists has to come from
the open data archives. These are annual ZIP files of XML, one document per
file, with the identifier as the filename.


``` r
etx_list_archives()
```

```
#> # A tibble: 6 x 4
#>   lang  year  name              size_mb
#>   <chr> <chr> <chr>               <dbl>
#> 1 et    2024  xml.2024.zip          344
#> 2 et    2025  xml.2025.zip         2640
#> 3 et    2026  xml.2026.zip        39700
#> 4 en    2024  xml.2024.en.zip        39
#> 5 en    2025  xml.2025.en.zip        70
#> 6 en    2026  xml.2026.en.zip      1010
```

The English set is about 1.1 GB in total, the Estonian set about 43 GB.
Nothing is downloaded unless asked for:


``` r
etx_download_corpus("en")

idx <- etx_list_documents("en")
nrow(idx)
head(idx)

etx_corpus_status()
```

Three properties of the archives shape how this works.

**They are complementary, not snapshots.** An annual folder holds the acts
published that year together with earlier acts that received a new version
during it, because they were amended or had an end of validity recorded.
Downloading only the newest year loses around 6% of the English corpus, so
`year = "all"` is the default.

**Coverage begins in 2024.** Acts still in force but unamended since then do
not appear in any archive. They remain retrievable by identifier through
`etx_get_doc()`, which has no such limit.

**They are large.** A HEAD request reports the total size of everything about
to be fetched. Above 5 GB an interactive session asks for confirmation and a
non-interactive one stops unless `force = TRUE`, which is what keeps
`etx_download_corpus("et")` from quietly pulling 43 GB.

Archives go to a temporary directory by default, so nothing is written
permanently without being asked for. To keep them between sessions, name a
directory and set an environment variable so that later sessions find it:


``` r
etx_download_corpus("en", dest = "~/estilex-corpus")

# In .Renviron, so that future sessions adopt it automatically
# ESTILEX_CORPUS_DIR=~/estilex-corpus
```

`etx_clear_corpus()` removes archives from the temporary directory. It leaves
a directory given through `dest` or the environment variable alone.

## What is not here

**Version enumeration.** An endpoint listing an act's consolidated versions
exists, but the Riigi Teataja has stated that interfaces built for the web
front end carry no public support. A package resting on one would be archived
when it breaks, without warning. Point-in-time work is possible wherever a
version identifier is known, as shown above; only enumerating versions is
unavailable.

**ELI identifiers.** The previous Riigi Teataja implemented
[ELI](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli-register/about.html), but the scheme did
not conform to the standard and was withdrawn in June 2026. The old URIs now
redirect to plain act addresses. estilex therefore offers no `eli` column,
rather than constructing something ELI-shaped that is not an ELI.

**Case law.** The API serves legislation. Court decisions are published
elsewhere and are out of scope here.

## Citing

Section 12 of the Riigi Teataja Act requires a reproduced text to cite the
published version. Every function returns `source_url`:


``` r
doc$source_url
#> [1] "https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/111042025003"
tr$source_url_en
#> [1] "https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/akt/523042025002"
```

## Related packages

estilex is part of lexverse, which follows the same conventions across
jurisdictions: a `status` column instead of exceptions, source-language field
names, identifiers as character, and `source_url` on every row.

- [eurlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=eurlex), EU law via Cellar
  SPARQL
- [finlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=finlex), Finland
- [swelex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=swelex), Sweden
- [danlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=danlex), Denmark
